BiblicalUsage: Rakkab is a charioteer, the man who drives the chariot. A certain man drew a bow at a venture and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness, and the chariot driver turned to carry him out of the host; and the watchman on the tower of Jezreel spied the company of Jehu as he came.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the charioteer is there at the turning points: the arrow found Ahab between the joints of his armour, and the watchman saw Jehu coming — and the driver could only carry the king away.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Jehu, King of Israel
